translations.idiomatic: Suibian Fort, formerly Zonggu, was built in the third year of Chongning (1104) and later renamed.

sentences.zh: 東至龍支城界六十里，西至宣威城界三十里，南至西寧州界三十二里，北至乳駱河界南一里。

translations.literal: East to Longzhi City border sixty li, west to Xuanwei City border thirty li, south to Xining Prefecture border thirty-two li, north to the Ruluo River border one li south.
translations.idiomatic: East to Longzhi City border, 60 li; west to Xuanwei City border, 30 li; south to Xining Prefecture border, 32 li; north to the Ruluo River border, 1 li south.

sentences.zh: 懷和砦，舊名丁令谷，崇寧三年置砦，賜名，又隸積石軍。

translations.literal: Huaihe Fort, formerly Dingling Valley; established as a fort in the third year of Chongning and named; also attached to Jishi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huaihe Fort, formerly Dingling Valley, was founded and named in the third year of Chongning (1104) and also placed under Jishi Army.

sentences.zh: 東至廓州界八十三里，西至青海一百三十餘里，南至順通堡界一十三里，北至清平砦界二十五里。

translations.literal: East to Kuo Prefecture border eighty-three li, west to Qinghai over one hundred thirty li, south to Shuntong Bastion border thirteen li, north to Qingping Fort border twenty-five li.
translations.idiomatic: East to Kuo Prefecture border, 83 li; west to Qinghai, over 130 li; south to Shuntong Bastion border, 13 li; north to Qingping Fort border, 25 li.

sentences.zh: 制羌砦。

translations.literal: Zhiqiang Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqiang Fort.

sentences.zh: 政和八年賜名。

translations.literal: Name bestowed in the eighth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Named in the eighth year of Zhenghe (1118).

sentences.zh: 地名曺猪氈嶺，屬西寧州。

translations.literal: The place is called Caozhu Zhan Ridge; belongs to Xining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Caozhu Zhan Ridge, under Xining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 震武軍。

translations.literal: Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，建築古骨龍城，賜名震武城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe Gugulong City was built and bestowed the name Zhenwu City.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenghe (1116) Gugulong City was built and named Zhenwu City.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改為震武軍。

translations.literal: Before long it was changed to Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it became Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 不見四至，據童貫奏，古骨龍元屬湟州。

translations.literal: The four boundaries are not recorded; according to Tong Guan's memorial, Gugulong originally belonged to Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Boundaries are not recorded; Tong Guan reported that Gugulong had originally belonged to Tang (Huang) Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 通濟橋，震武城浮橋，政和六年賜名。

translations.literal: Tongji Bridge, the Zhenwu City pontoon bridge; named in the sixth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Tongji Bridge, Zhenwu City's pontoon bridge, was named in the sixth year of Zhenghe (1116).

sentences.zh: 善治堡，政和六年，震武城通濟橋堡賜名。

translations.literal: Shanzhi Bastion: in the sixth year of Zhenghe the Zhenwu City Tongji Bridge bastion was bestowed the name Shanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhi Bastion: in the sixth year of Zhenghe (1116) Zhenwu City's Tongji Bridge bastion was named Shanzhi.

sentences.zh: 大同堡，本名古骨龍城應接堡，政和六年賜名。

translations.literal: Datong Bastion, originally the Gugulong City supporting bastion; named in the sixth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Datong Bastion, originally Gugulong City's supporting bastion, was named in the sixth year of Zhenghe (1116).

sentences.zh: 德通城，本瞎令古城，政和七年，劉法既解震武軍圍，建築，賜名。

translations.literal: Detong City, originally Xialing Old City; in the seventh year of Zhenghe, after Liu Fa lifted the siege of Zhenwu Army, it was built and named.
translations.idiomatic: Detong City, formerly Xialing Old City, was built and named in the seventh year of Zhenghe (1117) after Liu Fa relieved Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 石門堡。

translations.literal: Shimen Bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Shimen Bastion.

sentences.zh: 瞎令古城北，地名石門子，政和七年賜名。

translations.literal: North of Xialing Old City at the place called Shimenzi; named in the seventh year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: North of Xialing Old City at Shimenzi, named in the seventh year of Zhenghe (1117).

sentences.zh: 積石軍。

translations.literal: Jishi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi Army.

sentences.zh: 本溪哥城。

translations.literal: Originally Xige City.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Xige City.

sentences.zh: 元符間，為吐蕃溪巴溫所據。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfu period held by the Tibetan Xibawen.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfu it was held by the Tibetan Xibawen.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，臧征撲哥以城降，即其地建軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan Zangzheng Puge surrendered the city; an army was established on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daguan (1108) Zangzheng Puge surrendered the city and an army was founded there.

sentences.zh: 東至廓州界八十里，西至青海一百餘里，南至蓋龍峗八十里，北至西寧州界八十里。

translations.literal: East to Kuo Prefecture border eighty li, west to Qinghai over one hundred li, south to Gailong Hill eighty li, north to Xining Prefecture border eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: East to Kuo Prefecture border, 80 li; west to Qinghai, over 100 li; south to Gailong Hill, 80 li; north to Xining Prefecture border, 80 li.

sentences.zh: 懷和砦，已見「西寧州」。

translations.literal: Huaihe Fort—already seen under Xining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huaihe Fort—see Xining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東至廓州界八十五里，西至青海一百三十餘里，南至順通堡界一十三里，北至清平砦界二十五里。

translations.literal: East to Kuo Prefecture border eighty-five li, west to Qinghai over one hundred thirty li, south to Shuntong Bastion border thirteen li, north to Qingping Fort border twenty-five li.
translations.idiomatic: East to Kuo Prefecture border, 85 li; west to Qinghai, over 130 li; south to Shuntong Bastion border, 13 li; north to Qingping Fort border, 25 li.

sentences.zh: 順通堡，東至臨松堡一十二里，西至本軍一十八里，南至臨松堡二十五里，北至懷和砦界一十二里。

translations.literal: Shuntong Bastion: east to Linsong Bastion twelve li, west to this army eighteen li, south to Linsong Bastion twenty-five li, north to Huaihe Fort border twelve li.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntong Bastion: east to Linsong Bastion, 12 li; west to this army, 18 li; south to Linsong Bastion, 25 li; north to Huaihe Fort border, 12 li.

sentences.zh: 臨松堡。

translations.literal: Linsong Bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Linsong Bastion.

sentences.zh: 東至廓州界五十里，西至順通堡界一十二里，南至把拶公原界約六十里，北至黃河一十五里。

translations.literal: East to Kuo Prefecture border fifty li, west to Shuntong Bastion border twelve li, south to Bazha Gongyuan border about sixty li, north to the Yellow River fifteen li.
translations.idiomatic: East to Kuo Prefecture border, 50 li; west to Shuntong Bastion border, 12 li; south to Bazha Gongyuan border, about 60 li; north to the Yellow River, 15 li.

sentences.zh: 陝西路，蓋《禹貢》雍、梁、冀、豫四州之域，而雍州全得焉。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Circuit—roughly the territory of Yong, Liang, Ji, and Yu provinces in the Yugong, with Yong Province wholly obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Circuit covered the Yugong domains of Yong, Liang, Ji, and Yu, with all of Yong.

sentences.zh: 當東井、輿鬼之分，西接羌戎，東界潼、陝，南抵蜀、漢，北際朔方。

translations.literal: It lies in the divisions of Dongjing and Yugui; west it adjoins Qiang and Rong, east it borders Tong and Shaan, south it reaches Shu and Han, north it meets Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: It lay in the Dongjing and Yugui astral mansions; west to Qiang and Rong, east to Tong and Shaan, south to Shu and Han, north to Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 有銅、鹽、金、鐵之產，絲、枲、林、木之饒，其民慕農桑，好稼穡。

translations.literal: It has copper, salt, gold, and iron; abundance of silk, hemp, forests, and timber; the people esteem farming and sericulture and love the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: It produced copper, salt, gold, and iron; silk, hemp, forests, and timber; the people prized farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 鄮杜、南山，土地膏沃，二渠灌溉，兼有其利。

translations.literal: Fengdu and Nanshan have rich soil; the two canals irrigate and both bring their benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Fengdu and the southern hills had fertile soil; twin canals irrigated the plain.

sentences.zh: 大抵誇尚氣勢，多遊俠輕薄之風，甚者好鬥輕死。

translations.literal: Generally they prize bravado; many have the ways of wandering knights and frivolity, and in the extreme they love fighting and lightly face death.
translations.idiomatic: Generally they prized swagger; wandering bravado was common, and some fought readily and held life cheap.

sentences.zh: 蒲、解本隸河東，故其俗頗純厚。

translations.literal: Pu and Xie originally belonged to Hedong, so their customs are rather pure and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Xie, once under Hedong, kept comparatively plain and steady customs.

sentences.zh: 被邊之地，以鞍馬、射獵為事，其人勁悍而質木。

translations.literal: Border lands take saddle horses and hunting as their business; the people are tough and simple.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier saddle horses and hunting dominated; the people were hardy and plain.

sentences.zh: 梁泉少桑麻之利，布泉、鹽酪資於他郡。

translations.literal: Liangquan lacked mulberry and hemp; cloth currency, salt, and dairy came from other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Liangquan lacked mulberry and hemp; cloth, salt, and dairy came from other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上洛多淫祀，申以科禁，故其俗稍變。

translations.literal: Shangluo had many improper cults; prohibitions were enforced, so the customs changed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Shangluo had many illicit shrines; legal bans shifted the customs somewhat.

sentences.zh: 秦、隴、儀、渭、涇、原、邠、寧、鄜、延、環、慶等皆分兵屯守，以備不虞雲。

translations.literal: Qin, Long, Yi, Wei, Jing, Yuan, Bin, Ning, Fu, Yan, Huan, and Qing all posted divided garrisons to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Long, Yi, Wei, Jing, Yuan, Bin, Ning, Fu, Yan, Huan, and Qing all kept divided garrisons against surprise.
